extracted.intended_audience: American citizens, cultural reformers, writers, and young men and women interested in democratic character and national culture
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for cultivating the ideal democratic personality, culture, literature, education, and political life in the United States; advice aimed at producing robust, individualistic, and religiously grounded citizens and native arts. Focuses on physical, moral, civic, and cultural standards for a mass population rather than elite forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy prefers occupied, property-owning citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Democracy looks with suspicious, ill-satisfied eye upon the very poor, the ignorant, and on those out of business. She asks for men and women with occupations, well-off, owners of houses and acres, and with cash in the bank--and with some cravings for literature, too; and must have them, and hastens to make them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a practical requirement for the endurance and stability of republican democracy: a middling aggregate of property-owners and engaged workers is what democracy both wants and tends to produce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy must pervade manners, institutions, and culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you, too, O friend, suppose democracy was only for elections, for politics, and for a party name? I say democracy is only of use there that it may pass on and come to its flower and fruits in manners, in the highest forms of interaction between men, and their beliefs--in religion, literature, colleges, and schools--democracy in all public and private life, and in the army and navy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative standard: political reform is insufficient; genuine democracy requires cultural, educational, religious, and social embodiment across society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy as a training-school / life's gymnasium
rubrics_metrics.description: Political democracy, as it exists and practically works in America, with all its threatening evils, supplies a training-school for making first-class men. It is life's gymnasium, not of good only, but of all. We try often, though we fall back often. ... Whatever we do not attain, we at any rate attain the experiences of the fight, the hardening of the strong campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Struggle, contest, and civic engagement are positive pedagogical forces; experience and hardening matter more than polished success. This counsels valuing participation and trials as formative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuality (personalism) is indispensable counterbalance
rubrics_metrics.description: To democracy, the leveler, the unyielding principle of the average, is surely join'd another principle...This second principle is individuality, the pride and centripetal isolation of a human being in himself--identity--personalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civilization depends on rich, varied personalism; individuality must be nourished as the compensating balance-wheel to the leveling forces of democratic aggregate life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture programme must be practical, mass-oriented, and inclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: I should demand a programme of culture, drawn out, not for a single class alone, or for the parlors or lecture-rooms, but with an eye to practical life, the west, the working-men, the facts of farms and jack-planes and engineers, and of the broad range of the women also of the middle and working strata, and with reference to the perfect equality of women...It must have for its spinal meaning the formation of a typical personality of character, eligible to the uses of the high average of men--and not restricted by conditions ineligible to the masses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: culture limited to elites and parlors. Guidance: design education and aesthetic programs to serve practical life and the broad population, including women and workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: American literature and art should speak to the common people and national spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: I feel...that among our geniuses and talented writers or speakers, few or none have yet really spoken to this people, created a single image-making work for them, or absorb'd the central spirit and the idiosyncrasies which are theirs--and which, thus, in highest ranges, so far remain entirely uncelebrated, unexpress'd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative criterion for writers and artists: create native, image-making works that reflect and celebrate the democratic people rather than importing foreign courtly models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical robustness as core of the model personality
rubrics_metrics.description: To our model, a clear-blooded, strong-fibred physique, is indispensable; the questions of food, drink, air, exercise, assimilation, digestion, can never be intermitted. Out of these we descry a well-begotten selfhood--in youth, fresh, ardent...at maturity, brave, perceptive, under control...movements easy, the complexion showing the best blood, somewhat flush'd, breast expanded, an erect attitude, a voice whose sound outvies music, eyes of calm and steady gaze...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete checklist of bodily and health features to aim for: diet, exercise, posture, voice, countenance—physical conditions are foundational to moral and civic excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental enlargement with restraint against overemphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to the mental-educational part of our model, enlargement of intellect, stores of cephalic knowledge, &c., the concentration thitherward of all the customs of our age, especially in America, is so overweening...it really needs nothing from us here--except, indeed, a phrase of warning and restraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educative ideal: cultivate intellect but beware excessive refinement that may crowd out native personality; manners flow from deeper causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand style flows from native personality, not mere cultured manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a man, artist or whoever, has health, pride, acuteness, noble aspirations, he has the motive-elements of the grandest style. The rest is but manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic standard: prioritize formation of core qualities (health, pride, acuteness, aspiration) over artificial stylistic training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscience and simple primary morality are essential
rubrics_metrics.description: I mean the simple, unsophisticated Conscience, the primary moral element. If I were asked to specify in what quarter lie the grounds of darkest dread...I should have to point to this particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral criterion: without invariable application of conscience to individuality, civilization is an amputation; this is the most worrying deficiency to remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion as inward, individual experience rather than institutional dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion...does not depend at all upon [churches], but is a part of the identified soul...Only in the perfect uncontamination and solitariness of individuality may the spirituality of religion positively come forth at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious ideal: cultivate interior religiousness via solitary reflection and identity; organized forms are secondary to inward communion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active political participation and independence from party machines
rubrics_metrics.description: To practically enter into politics is an important part of American personalism...I advise every young man to do so. Always inform yourself; always do the best you can; always vote. Disengage yourself from parties. ...steadily hold yourself judge and master over all of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civic guideline: engage in politics, be informed, vote, but resist blind party allegiance; parties can usurp government and be corrupt or savage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full equality and practical roles for women in democratic life
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea of the women of America...develop'd, raised to become the robust equals, workers, and, it may be, even practical and political deciders with the men--greater than man, we may admit, through their divine maternity...but great, at any rate, as man, in all departments; or, rather, capable of being so, soon as they realize it, and can bring themselves to give up toys and fictions, and launch forth, as men do, amid real, independent, stormy life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic criterion: advocate for women's full participation and equality; prepare social structures and culture to support robust female personalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical labor for women is dignified and compatible with womanhood
rubrics_metrics.description: She soon became an expert seamstress...She has told me that she finds nothing degrading in her position; it is not inconsistent with personal dignity, self-respect, and the respect of others...She has made herself understood, and preserves her independence...and her course of life is not without opportunities for mental improvement, and of much quiet, uncosting happiness and love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative examples of acceptable working-woman roles: seamstress, housekeeper, mechanical business operator, wife-mother who makes domestic duties illustrious—anti-pattern is treating such work as degrading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current 'culture' risks producing supercilious infidels
rubrics_metrics.description: As now taught, accepted and carried out, are not the processes of culture rapidly creating a class of supercilious infidels, who believe in nothing? Shall a man lose himself in countless masses of adjustments...that the simply good and healthy and brave parts of him are reduced and clipp'd away?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique: elite-focused refinement and polite conformity can corrupt belief and vitality; culture must be reoriented to practical, robust values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fruition of democracy will be judged in the long-run by produced characters
rubrics_metrics.description: I submit...that the fruition of democracy, on aught like a grand scale, resides altogether in the future. ...the only large and satisfactory justification of it resides in the future, mainly through the copious production of perfect characters among the people, and through the advent of a sane and pervading religiousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historic/teleological criterion: assess democracy by whether it ultimately generates exemplary individual characters and pervasive spiritual life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve a balance: allow healthy rudeness and unpolished virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision for a little healthy rudeness, savage virtue, justification of what one has in one's self, whatever it is, is demanded. Negative qualities, even deficiencies, would be a relief. Singleness and normal simplicity and separation...we would welcome their return!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural recommendation: resist over-polish; tolerate robust, rudimentary traits that preserve vigor and individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentage/upbringing must proactively shape future personalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Parentage must consider itself in advance. (Will the time hasten when fatherhood and motherhood shall become a science--and the noblest science?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction: plan early for physical and moral formation (food, air, exercise, etc.); view parenthood as an active, scientific responsibility in producing desired citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject imported European caste-based models; develop native American types
rubrics_metrics.description: America has yet morally and artistically originated nothing. She seems singularly unaware that the models of persons, books, manners, &c., appropriate for former conditions and for European lands, are but exiles and exotics here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural policy: create new native prototypes of personhood and art suitable to American democratic conditions instead of copying aristocratic European models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular judgment and civic trial correct elected failures over time
rubrics_metrics.description: What is more dramatic than the spectacle...the popular judgment taking the successful candidates on trial in the offices...and always giving, finally, the fit, exactly due reward? ...a well-contested American national election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political standard: trust in the corrective capacity of popular scrutiny and elections; accept temporary incompetence as part of democratic learning.
